Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.262/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vatakara is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience,
the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Sections 140 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 21.11.2009.

According to the petitioner, on 21.11.2009 at about 11 a.m., while he was riding a motor cycle through the public road, a stage carriage bearing registration No.KL-58- 9333 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit on his motor cycle and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:16680 offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.7,00,000/- (subsequently enhanced to Rs.20,00,000/-).
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A15 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,05,483/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

sentences.text:
9. Heard Sri. V. N. Ramesan Nambisan., the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant,
and Sri. Rajit, the learned Standing 2025:KER:16680 Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that though the petitioner proved his monthly salary as Rs.14,410/- through Exhibits A13, A14 and A15 documents, the Tribunal has not awarded any compensation on the head loss of disability on the ground that he is continuing as a teacher and getting salary without any reduction.

Relying upon the decision of a Single Bench of this Court in Raju Sebastian v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. [2021 (5) KHC 662],
he argued that in the case of permanent employees, getting monthly salary, for the purpose of assessing the loss of disability, 50% of the salary drawn on the date of accident is to be taken as the notional income.

entities.text: Raju Sebastian v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. [2021 (5) KHC 662]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do not find any grounds to reject the above argument, in the light of the above decision.

Since as per Exhibits A13, 14 and 15 the monthly salary of the petitioner is Rs.14,410/-,
50% of the same will come to Rs.7,205/- and it fixed as the notional income of the petitioner.

11. In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"Fracture (right) femur middle shaft open type IIIA, fracture 2025:KER:16680 tibial plateau (right), fracture both bone (right) leg distal 1/3rd, fracture greater tuberosity (right) shoulder, a severe injury"
12.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 154 days and outpatient treatment is still continuing.
He has produced additional medical bills as Annexure A1 to A103, together worth Rs.66,375/-.
It shows that he is even now continuing the treatment on account of the injuries sustained in the accident.
13. The Tribunal fixed his permanent physical disability at 26%.

However, as per the disability certificate produced by him, along with Annexures, issued by the medical board constituted by the Superintendent, Government District Hospital, Vatakara, his permanent physical disability is assessed as 50%.

Since the petitioner is continuing his treatment even now, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the disability certificate issued by the Medical Board and produced by him along with the Annexures and it is marked as Exhibit C1, for reference.
Accordingly, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 50%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 31 years.

Therefore, 50% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 16, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.10,37,520/-.
15. The petitioner appeared before the Court.
He has shown his right leg, from which it can be seen that the injuries sustained in the accident are still not healed.

He could walk only with difficulty,
even at present.

sentences.text: Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.50,000/-.

Another sum of Rs.10,000/- was awarded towards disfiguration of whole body, Rs.15,000/- towards mental shock and agony, Rs.25,000/- towards future treatment, and Rs.24,800/- towards bystander expenses.

No separate amount is seen awarded on the head 'loss of amenities of life'.
17.
The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 154 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the 2025:KER:16680 petitioner, and also considering the fact that even now he is continuing treatment for the injuries sustained in the accident, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', 'loss of amenities of life',
and 'Bystander expenses' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-,
Rs.2,00,000/- and Rs.35,000/- respectively.
The amount awarded on the head 'mental shock and agony' will be deducted.

18. Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient for 154 days, towards loss of earning, he is entitled to get the salary for a period of 6 months, which will come to Rs.86460/- (14410 x 6).
19.
Towards 'future medical expenses', only Rs.25,000/- is seen awarded by the Tribunal.
Even during the pendency of the appeal, petitioner has produced medical bills worth Rs.66,375/-.
In addition to the same as per I.A. No.1 of 2025, he has produced additional bills worth Rs.4118/-.

Therefore, towards additional medical expenses he is entitled for Rs.70,493/- (66375+4118).
20.
Considering the fact that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are still live, he requires compensation for future treatment.

Therefore, 2025:KER:16680 Rs.25,000/- awarded on that head is on the lower side and hence it is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-
21.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

22. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.21,20,156/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
